intro:
By this sign: the Komuch offensive

June 8th, 1918

The men coming down the Volga have a banner with the old words on it - By this sign shalt thou conquer - and underneath the banner is a Committee of ex-deputies, a Czechoslovak corps that was supposed to be going home through Vladivostok, and the officers' druzhinas of every town between here and Chelyabinsk. They are going to write those words over everything they take. We shall see what they are worth by the autumn.

Samara fell this morning. The Czechoslovak battalions took the bridge over the Volga before the demolition party got to it, and the Committee of Members of the Constituent Assembly has declared itself the government of Russia in a building the garrison was holding at breakfast.

I command a detachment of the 1st Army. Between Samara and Kazan there is one railway, four towns on it, and nothing else. Hold them, and take the bridgehead back if it can be done.

Victory conditions:
- Hold Simbirsk (7,5), Melekess (21,7), Stavropol (20,19) and Syzran (8,26).
- Take Samara (30,23).

briliant.text:
The four towns are held and the line between them is ours. We did not get Samara back - the bridgehead was reinforced across the river faster than we could close it, and a frontal attack over that bridge with the troops available would have cost the detachment and bought nothing.

The Eastern Front is being organised properly at last: Vatsetis is forming it into armies with staffs and a supply service instead of detachments that answer to whoever raised them. What we have given him is a front that still exists to be organised.

lose.text:
The railway line has gone with the towns on it. The detachments that were holding it are coming north as best they can, most of them without their guns.

The Volga from Syzran to Melekess is theirs, and Kazan is now the front line.

intro:
Uncountable trophies: Kazan

August 4th, 1918

Kazan holds the gold.

Six hundred million roubles of the Imperial reserve were evacuated here for safety in 1915 and they are still in the bank vaults, and every man in Kappel's column knows it. That is why the attack is coming here and not somewhere sensible, and it is also why we cannot simply trade the city for space.

Kappel has perhaps three thousand men and the Serbian battalion and two gunboats. We have the 5th Army, which is three days old and has a staff that has never worked together. Hold the Kremlin, the academy and the river crossings. Bogorodskoye downstream is where their flotilla is basing.

Victory conditions:
- Hold the Kazan Kremlin (27,3), the Military Academy (26,2), Vasilyevo (22,3), Verkhniy Uslan (23,4) and Karaishevo (33,17).
- Take Bogorodskoye (30,25).

briliant.text:
Kazan is held, the vaults are intact, and the flotilla base downstream has been burned out from the land side.

Trotsky's train is at Sviyazhsk and the Fifth Army has been given a spine in a week: field courts, commissars in every regiment, and reinforcements coming up the line from Moscow. The gold stays where it is until it can be moved under guard.

The Committee's people are calling this their high-water mark in the newspapers. They are about to be right.

Our army has fallen back on Sviyazhsk. Trotsky's train arrived there this morning and the first thing off it was a field tribunal.

intro:
Harvest of sorrow: the end of the Komuch

September 18th, 1918

The tide has turned and the Committee knows it before we do.

Kazan was retaken on the tenth, Simbirsk on the twelfth - Tukhachevsky's 1st Army took it in two days and sent Lenin a telegram about it while he was still in bed with a bullet in him. The People's Army is coming apart: the mobilised peasants will not fight for the Committee, and the Czechoslovaks have decided they are going home after all and would rather not die on the Volga first.

Samara and Syzran are the last of it. The Committee's staff and its treasury are already loading at Krotovka to go east to Ufa, and every column that gets out will be in the line against us again in the spring under Kolchak.

Victory conditions:
- Take Samara (30,23) and Syzran (8,26).
- Hold Simbirsk (8,6).
- The enemy escapes instead if seven of his columns get out through Krotovka (41,23).

briliant.text:
Samara and Syzran are ours. The Committee of Members of the Constituent Assembly ceased to govern anything at about two o'clock this afternoon.

Much of their staff got away east - the trains at Krotovka were loaded and moving before our cavalry reached the yard, and a railway is a hard thing to catch. What did not get away was the People's Army, which has stopped existing as a formation. The Volga is Soviet from Nizhny to Astrakhan.

In Omsk, meanwhile, they have decided that committees were the problem. There is talk of a Supreme Ruler.

lose.text:
The evacuation went off complete: staff, treasury, printing presses and the greater part of the People's Army, east along the Ufa line.

We hold Simbirsk and the middle Volga, which is the campaign's object and not much comfort tonight. Everything that left Krotovka this week will be in front of us at Ufa.

intro:
At the gates of Europe: Ufa

January 6th, 1919

There is a Supreme Ruler now.

Admiral Kolchak took power in Omsk in November by arresting the last of the Committee's ministers, and the Entente has recognised what he did by continuing to unload rifles at Vladivostok. He has a real staff, a real mobilisation and the whole of Siberia's railway.

His first stroke has come at Ufa in a Urals winter, against the 5th Army, which is holding a hundred and fifty versts with nine thousand men and no reserve worth the name. It is thirty degrees below and the ground cannot be dug.

Hold the city and the approaches. Iglino on the Chelyabinsk line is where their assault groups form.

Victory conditions:
- Hold Ufa (3,17), Cherkassy (11,2), Kumlekul (6,4) and Alatorka (21,18).
- Take Iglino (37,21).

briliant.text:
Ufa is held and the forming-up area at Iglino was broken up before their main body could use it.

The front will still be shortened. Not because of this sector: the Perm direction has gone - the 3rd Army lost eighteen thousand men and the city on Christmas Eve - and a line that holds in the centre while its right is walked round is a line that gets encircled. We go back on the Ufa river in good order and with the army intact.

A commission from Moscow is on its way to find out what happened at Perm. Stalin and Dzerzhinsky, they say.

victory.text:

lose.text:
The city has gone, and the Ufa river with it. The 5th Army is falling back on Sterlitamak in weather that is killing more of the wounded than the fighting did.

Perm went a fortnight ago. The whole Urals front is now a line drawn on a map in Moscow and not much else.

intro:
Breakthrough: the spring offensive

March 1st, 1919

This is the one they have been building all winter.

Khanzhin's Western Army has come out of the thaw straight at the junction of our 5th and 1st Armies with a three-to-one superiority on the axis of attack, and behind it Gaida is driving on Vyatka to join hands with the interventionists at Archangel. If those two ever shake hands the northern half of the Republic is cut off.

We have five towns on the railway and not enough of anything. Hold them. Ufa, behind their front, is their railhead and their whole supply rests on it.

Victory conditions:
- Hold Belebei (12,16), Tuymazy (8,7), Abdulino (8,22), Sterlitamak (32,22) and Meleuz (32,28).
- Take Ufa (33,4).

briliant.text:
The five towns are still ours and their timetable is a fortnight behind.

That fortnight is the whole value of what was done here. The Central Committee has declared the Eastern Front the decisive front; Frunze is forming a southern group at Buzuluk out of everything the Republic can scrape together, and every day their offensive spends grinding against these towns is a day that group gets stronger and their own flank gets longer.

lose.text:
The junction was broken open and the towns went one after another. Their cavalry is between our two armies and there is no continuous front left on this sector.

Frunze's group at Buzuluk will have to be committed early, into a battle it did not choose.

intro:
Rush: the spring offensive

March 14th, 1919

They have not stopped, and now there is nothing behind us to stop them with.

Khanzhin is driving for the Volga and Samara and he is doing it with everything at once, on a front too wide for his own supply, because he has been told the Volga must be reached before the Southern Front's own offensive begins. Our task is to make him pay for every verst and to still be holding these towns when his momentum runs out.

There is no counterattack in these orders. There is a clock, and a line of towns, and the requirement that both still be ours when the clock stops.

Victory conditions:
- When the time runs out, hold six objectives for a brilliant victory, five for a victory, four for a tactical victory.
- The objectives are Ufa (33,4), Tuymazy (8,7), Belebei (12,16), Abdulino (8,22), Sterlitamak (32,22) and Meleuz (32,28).

briliant.text:
The line is still on the map and the towns named in my orders are still ours. Their leading regiments have outrun their own trains and are living off the villages, which in this province is the fastest way to lose a village.

Frunze's group is complete at Buzuluk. The southern group attacks in April.

victory.text:

lose.text:
They are through. The towns are gone and the leading Cossack patrols were within a hundred versts of the Volga before the thaw stopped them rather than we did.

Everything now depends on Frunze's group being ready before they are.

intro:
Song of the Cossacks: Orenburg

April 17th, 1919

Orenburg has been under siege, on and off, for most of a year.

Dutov's Orenburg Cossacks want it because without it their Host has no capital and no junction; we hold it because it is the only rail link to Turkestan and to the Soviet republics beyond it. Cut that and Central Asia is on its own.

The garrison is the town: railwaymen, the Kirghiz and Tatar detachments, a workers' regiment, and the 1st Army's left flank. The relieving force is going to Buzuluk instead, because Frunze is about to attack, and I would rather he did.

Hold the ring. There is one gap in their line, north of the river, and it may be worth closing.

Victory conditions:
- When the time runs out, hold five objectives for a brilliant victory, four for a victory, three for a tactical victory.
- The objectives are Orenburg (8,30), Sakmara (16,19), Seitovsky Posad (10,21), Nizhnie Chebenki (24,18) and Verkhnie Chebenki (29,18).
- Or take their crossing at (24,4).

briliant.text:
The ring held. The road to Turkestan is open and the trains are running again, which means grain and cotton for the Republic and ammunition for Frunze.

Dutov has been drawing regiments off Kolchak's own flank to sit outside this town for a year. Long may he continue.

intro:
Clutching at straws: Belebei

May 15th, 1919

Now we attack, and we attack quickly, because the whole point of this is that they should not have time to think.

Frunze's southern group has already broken the Western Army at Buguruslan and Bugulma. Khanzhin is trying to reform on the Belebei position with his Volga Corps, which is the old People's Army under a new name and is being asked to do the work of two corps.

The 25th Rifle Division under Chapayev goes in first. There is very little time: everything here depends on hitting the position before it becomes one.

Victory conditions:
- Take Belebei (12,16), Tuymazy (8,7), Buzdyak (16,7) and Shafranovo (19,14) - four turns for a brilliant victory, seven for a victory, ten at the outside.
- Hold Abdulino (8,22).

briliant.text:
All four in the time allowed. The Volga Corps has been broken up as a formation and its trains are ours, and the road to Ufa is open.

Their spring offensive is finished. From here the Eastern Front does not defend.

victory.text:
All four in the time allowed. The Volga Corps has been broken up as a formation and its trains are ours, and the road to Ufa is open.

Their spring offensive is finished. From here the Eastern Front does not defend.

lose.text:
We took the ground and took too long doing it. Their corps got back across the Belaya with its artillery and will be waiting for us on the far bank.

The offensive continues, but the cheap part of it is over.

intro:
The tide turns: Chistopol

May 26th, 1919

This is the point on which the whole summer turns, and I would rather it were somewhere with better roads.

North of us Gaida's Siberian Army is still pushing on Vyatka and has not yet understood that the army on its left has collapsed. If we take Bugulma and the Azanakayevo junction now, that whole northern group is fighting with a hole where its flank used to be and the Urals are open to us.

If we do not - if this attack fails and their reserves come south in time - then it is their offensive again, and it will be aimed at the Volga crossings, and I shall be fighting it in front of Kazan.

Victory conditions:
- Take Bugulma (25,20) and Azanakayevo (28,17).
- Hold Chistopol (6,9), Naberezhnye Chelny (23,4) and Menzelinsk (28,4).

briliant.text:
Bugulma and the junction are ours. Gaida's flank is open and he has finally been told to stop.

The front headquarters has confirmed the next objective and it is the one everybody has been waiting for: across the Belaya, and Ufa.

victory.text:
Bugulma and the junction are ours. Gaida's flank is open and he has finally been told to stop.

The front headquarters has confirmed the next objective and it is the one everybody has been waiting for: across the Belaya, and Ufa.

tactical.text:

lose.text:
The attack was held and then thrown back, and their reserves are coming south by rail faster than we can reform.

The initiative has gone with them. Kazan is being put into a state of defence and I am ordered there tonight.

intro:
We'll never leave again: Kazan

June 10th, 1919

Twice in one year is more than any city should be asked for.

Our attack in May was held and the counterstroke that followed it has carried them back onto the Volga. Kazan is again the front line: the Kremlin, the academy, the crossings, and behind them the road to Nizhny.

The front is being rebuilt around this city while we hold it. Every division that comes up the line arrives because we were still here when it started loading.

Victory conditions:
- When the time runs out, hold six objectives for a brilliant victory, five for a victory, four for a tactical victory.
- The objectives are the Kazan Kremlin (27,3), the Military Academy (26,2), Vasilyevo (22,3), Zelenodolsk (14,1), Teteyevo (28,18), Bogorodskoye (30,25) and the crossing at (9,26).
- Or take Bolshiye Kabany (32,9) and Pelevo (36,13).

briliant.text:
Kazan is held and their thrust has broken on it. Their army has spent the reserves it brought south and has nothing behind them.

The crisis is over. The front headquarters is putting the offensive back together on the old axis, and my orders send me east again - to the Belaya and Ufa, where this should have gone a month ago.

victory.text:

lose.text:
The Kremlin quarter was lost and the crossings with it. We are going back down the Volga line towards Samara, and the army is going with us.

Samara is the next place with a bridge.

intro:
Where it all began: Samara

July 14th, 1919

A year and a month since the Czechoslovaks took this bridge, and here we are arguing over it again.

Their advance down the Volga has not been stopped so much as slowed, and the front headquarters is moving its staffs between three threatened directions by rail, which is what happens when a front has more axes than reserves. My group has been sent here.

Hold the crossings. Melekess and Krotovka, upstream and east, are their staging points; either would be worth taking off them.

Victory conditions:
- When the time runs out, hold three objectives for a brilliant victory, two for a victory or a tactical victory.
- The objectives are Samara (30,23), Simbirsk (7,5) and Syzran (8,26).
- Or take Melekess (21,7) and Krotovka (41,23).

briliant.text:
The crossings are ours and their staging areas have been cleared. The Volga line holds.

The offensive can be restarted on the proper axis. I am ordered east to rejoin the drive on Ufa.

victory.text:
The crossings are ours and their staging areas have been cleared. The Volga line holds.

The offensive can be restarted on the proper axis. I am ordered east to rejoin the drive on Ufa.

tactical.text:

The offensive can be restarted on the proper axis. I am ordered east to rejoin the drive on Ufa.

lose.text:
Samara has gone. The bridge was blown behind the last of our columns, which is the one thing on my list that got done properly.

The staff is being moved north to Vyatka. So am I.

intro:
No mercy: Vyatka

October 20th, 1919

Gaida is gone - Kolchak dismissed him in the summer and he has since tried to overthrow his own government in Vladivostok - but the Siberian Army's northern drive has been picked up by someone else, and it still wants what it always wanted: Vyatka, and a junction with the interventionists coming down from Archangel.

If they meet, the Republic is cut in half along the Northern Dvina and everything north of Moscow is on the wrong side of the line.

Hold the three city sectors and Karavayevy. Vakhrushi is their forward railhead.

Victory conditions:
- When the time runs out, hold four objectives for a brilliant victory, three for a victory, two for a tactical victory.
- The objectives are the three Vyatka sectors (27,10), (24,16), (22,18) and Karavayevy (11,18).
- Or take Vakhrushi (40,8).

briliant.text:
Vyatka holds and the two halves of their northern plan are still two hundred versts apart. The British at Archangel are loading their own transports; they will not be coming south for anybody.

The front can be restored on the main axis. East, to Ufa.

victory.text:

lose.text:
The city sectors were lost one by one over four days. What is left of the group is going south-west on the Kotelnich road.

The next place they can be stopped is Saratov, which tells you how far this has gone.

intro:
The Black Baron: Saratov

November 13th, 1919

The Eastern Front now has a southern neighbour, and the neighbour has arrived.

Wrangel's Caucasus Army has come up the Volga from Tsaritsyn to shake hands with Kolchak's people, which is the one thing both White commands have wanted all year and have never managed to arrange. Our task is to see that they do not manage it here either.

Saratov is two sectors and a river frontage, with Atkarsk covering the railway west. Volsk upstream is where their two forces are trying to link.

Victory conditions:
- When the time runs out, hold three objectives for a brilliant victory or a victory, two for a tactical victory.
- The objectives are the two Saratov sectors (16,12), (19,13) and Atkarsk (3,3).
- Or take Volsk (37,1).

briliant.text:
They have not linked up. Saratov is ours, the railway west is open, and the two White armies remain what they have been all year: two armies.

Front headquarters is turning the offensive back east. Ufa next, and this time properly.

victory.text:
They have not linked up. Saratov is ours, the railway west is open, and the two White armies remain what they have been all year: two armies.

Front headquarters is turning the offensive back east. Ufa next, and this time properly.

lose.text:
Saratov has gone. The link-up they wanted has been made and there is a continuous White front from the Volga to the Urals for the first time in this war.

I am ordered to Ryazan with what I can bring out.

intro:
Mousetrap: Ryazan

December 12th, 1919

Ryazan is not a front-line town. It is where the roads from the south and the east meet before Moscow, and that is why I am standing in it in December with a group made of other people's spare regiments.

Five objectives, a river, and a railway junction. If this line goes there is one more behind it and then there is Moscow.

Venev, on the Tula road, is where their forward group has come up. It is worth a great deal to us and probably not much to them yet.

Victory conditions:
- When the time runs out, hold five objectives for a brilliant victory, four for a victory, three for a tactical victory.
- The objectives are Ryazan (34,5), Kolomna (4,4), Turlatovo (41,11), Plakhino (35,19) and Kashira (2,24).
- Or take Venev (6,36).

briliant.text:
The junction is held and their forward group has been pushed off the Tula road. The reserves that were forming behind us have not had to be spent covering a retreat, which means they can be used for something.

The front is going over to the offensive again on the eastern axis. My group entrains tomorrow.

victory.text:

lose.text:
The junction is theirs. We are going north-west along the last railway we still hold.

Klin is the next station with anything to hold on to.

intro:
As though nothing could fall: Klin

December 30th, 1919

There is nothing behind this one.

Klin is on the Petrograd railway sixty versts from Moscow. Everything the Republic has been able to scrape together in a fortnight is in the line here: the courses cadets, two workers' regiments from the Moscow factories, the internationalist battalion, and the regiments that have been retreating since Saratov and are being asked to stop today.

Five towns. Hold them until the clock runs out. Their forward staging area is south of us and if it can be taken, take it.

Victory conditions:
- When the time runs out, hold five objectives for a brilliant victory, four for a victory, three for a tactical victory.
- The objectives are Klin (11,6), Woronino (19,3), Rogatschewo (29,7), Fedoroloka (27,16) and Solnogorsk (16,18).
- Or take their staging area at (19,28).

briliant.text:
It held. Their attack has stopped in front of Klin and this morning their forward units were reported moving back.

They cannot stay where they are: a front that long, in winter, at the end of a single railway with partisans on it, does not hold together once it stops moving forward. The reserves that were built up behind this line are intact and they are going east.

Back to the proper war. Ufa is in my orders and I have been waiting a long time to read that word again.

The line is broken and there is no other. I am writing this from a train that is not going to stop anywhere useful.

Whatever is decided now will be decided by people other than us.

intro:
Peace through strength: Zhitomir

May 19th, 1920

During 1919 Poland was a formidable foe for the Red Army, that tried in vain to expand to the west only to be defeated by the brave Poles. I am convinced that, were it not for Poland, the Bolsheviks would have reached the borders of Germany, Hungary and other countries, where they would have instigated successful communist revolutions. Most people in Europe don't realise how much they owe to Poland, that acted as a barrier to the Soviet expansion. Personally, I respect and appreciate what the Poles did.

However, the respect that we had for the Polish army, and the fact that the Bolsheviks were our common enemies for many months, couldn't hide the mutual enmity that existed between us. We knew that, once the Red Army was finally destroyed, Poland would become our new main enemy, at least in the short term.

But I must be clear about this: in 1920 we didn't want a war with Poland. Kolchak was resigned to accept the demands of the League of Nations and to leave the Poles alone. It was them who, blinded by their victories against the Bolsheviks, believed that they could force us to leave Belarus and Ukraine, where they would support the establishment of independent republics that (of course!) would be allies of Poland and enemies of Russia.

And that was how, in April 1920, Poland invaded Ukraine. Naturally, that act of aggression against us was condemned by the League of Nations, whose delegates made us know that if Russia used an armed force against the Polish Army, only for defensive purposes, the League would support us. That was all that Kolchak wanted, and he immediately sent an army to Volinia, in western Ukraine, in order to stop the Polish invasion.

Victory conditions:
- Take all the VHs.

briliant.text:
Our victory was complete. The Polish were routed, and they retreated so fast that I think we could have reached Warsaw in a few weeks if we had wanted to. Instead, we contented ourselves with the liberation of most of Belarus and Ukraine and with reasonable war reparations. The Poles agreed to our conditions, and both sides signed a peace treaty in Minsk in June 1920.

Russia had nearlly collapsed during those chaotic years, but in the end we managed to salvage most of our country. Since then we have worked hard to improve Russia and its people, rejecting all marxist ideas. There is still a lot left to do, and many unsolved problems, but at least we have hope in the future. May God help Russia and her rulers, so our country can thrive and we never engage again in nightmarish civil wars.

The campaign is over. I hope you've liked it and thanks for playing.

Urica, 2018

lose.text:
The Poles surprised us and defeated us, reaching Kiev a couple of weeks later. The risk of a new Bolshevik uprising was high, so we had to accept humiliating peace conditions, which included the acknowledgement of the independence of Poland, Belarus and Ukraine.

Ashamed for my failure, I left the army and went back to Samara, where I found a job as a teacher. Luckily, people soon forgot about me. After all, I'm not the first Russian officer who fails at a very critical moment. At least I can proudly say that we defeated the Bolsheviks and that, although the empire has been lost, Russia still has a future thanks to people like me. I did my best to serve my country. I wish I had done it better, but I couldn't. Over time, I have learnt to live with that.

intro:
Farewell to Ufa

May 29th, 1919

Across the Belaya, then.

The Western Army is broken and the town it has been supplying itself from all spring is on the far bank of a wide river with one bridge. Chapayev's 25th Division goes across on rafts and pontoons north of the city; the rest of the group goes for the Chishmy junction to cut the line out.

There is no reserve and no second attempt. Twelve turns is what the front headquarters has given us, and it has given the same twelve turns to their rearguard.

Victory conditions:
- Take Ufa (33,4) and Chishmy (22,7) within twelve turns.
- Hold Buzdyak (16,7) and Sterlitamak (32,22).

briliant.text:
Ufa is ours and the Chishmy junction with it. Their army went east along the Zlatoust line at night with what it could carry.

The Urals are open. Chapayev was gassed from the air over the crossing and refused to be taken off the field; he is in the line today.

Next is the passes, and after the passes, Siberia.

The crossing was forced but the junction held, and their rearguard used the time to get the trains out to Zlatoust.

The city is ours. Their army is not.

intro:
Ekaterinburg

July 12th, 1919

A year and a week since the house on Voznesensky Lane, and we shall be the ones who have to find out what happened in it.

The 2nd and 3rd Armies have come over the northern Urals and Ekaterinburg is the prize: the junction of everything, the Verkh-Isetsk works, and the last real city before Siberia proper.

Their evacuation began before our guns were in range. Six marked columns of staff, treasury and archives are trying to get out on the Tyumen line, and what is in them will decide what anyone is able to prove about this year afterwards.

Victory conditions:
- Take Ekaterinburg (15,3).
- Hold Severskiy (6,19) and Davydova (34,21).
- The enemy escapes instead if six of his columns get out at (36,9).

briliant.text:
Ekaterinburg is taken. The works are intact - they had the demolition charges laid and no time to fire them.

Sokolov's investigation papers, or what our people could stop of them, are with the tribunal. I have read enough of the summary to be glad the rest is somebody else's work.

The road east is the Trans-Siberian and there is very little on it now that can stop an army.

The city is ours and the trains are gone - every one of the marked columns out on the Tyumen line while we were still fighting for the station approaches.

The 3rd Army has been badly cut about doing it and the pursuit will have to wait for it to be made up. The front headquarters has asked me some sharp questions and they are fair ones.

intro:
Chelyabinsk

July 25th, 1919

We took this city four days ago and now we have to keep it, which the enemy has evidently decided is a different question.

The 5th Army came through the passes and into Chelyabinsk on the twenty-fourth. Kolchak's staff has been planning exactly this: let the Reds into the town, close on both flanks from Miasskoye and the north, and destroy an army in a street it thinks it owns.

So they will come, and they will come at both shoulders at once. The city rose to help us take it - the railway workshops turned out three regiments in a week - and those men are in the line now.

Victory conditions:
- When the time runs out, hold six objectives for a brilliant victory, five for a victory, four for a tactical victory.
- The objectives are Chelyabinsk (25,11), Argayash (14,4), Dolgoderevenskoye (22,6), Poletaevo (20,16), Chebarkul (7,17) and Yemanzhelinsk (23,22).
- Or take Miasskoye (32,7).

briliant.text:
Both pincers were broken and the city is ours. Their counterstroke was their last army reserve in the Urals and it has been spent.

There is no natural line between here and the Tobol. The pursuit goes on into Siberia.

victory.text:

There is no natural line between here and the Tobol. The pursuit goes on into Siberia.

lose.text:
The pincers closed north of the city and the army had to fight its way west out of a town it had taken. The workshop regiments covered the withdrawal and most of them did not come out.

The Urals will have to be done again.

intro:
Not dead yet: the Tobol (I)

September 1st, 1919

They are not finished, and the men who told the front headquarters they were finished should come and look at this.

Kolchak's armies have been reorganised behind the Tobol - Dieterichs has combed out the rear areas, the Siberian Cossacks have been mobilised wholesale, and they have counted correctly that our own divisions are down to half strength and six hundred versts from their railhead.

The blow has fallen on our left, where the Cossack cavalry has the open steppe. Hold the line of villages. Petropavlovsk behind their front is the objective everything else here is a step towards.

Victory conditions:
- When the time runs out, hold four objectives for a brilliant victory, three for a victory, two for a tactical victory.
- The objectives are Makushino (4,4), Petukhovo (15,7), Mamlyutka (27,9) and Presnovka (4,18).
- Or take Petropavlovsk (38,12).

briliant.text:
The line held through the whole of their effort. They have put in their last mobilised reserves against these villages and they have not moved us off them.

Our own reinforcements are coming up the line at last. The counterstroke on the Tobol is being prepared and it will not have to start from behind a river.

victory.text:

lose.text:
We were pushed back off the villages and over the Tobol. Their cavalry is loose on the steppe behind our left.

The line will have to be restored on the river, and restoring it is the next task.

intro:
Better to burn out: the Tobol (II)

September 25th, 1919

Their offensive is a month old and it is running on nothing.

Every mobilised recruit they put into the line this month has been taken from a village that is now sending its sons to the partisans instead. Their supply comes down one railway with the Siberian partisan detachments sitting on it. They have gained ground and lost the army that gained it.

We hold the Kurgan crossings and the Tobol bank. Their two forward groups east of the river are what is left of their striking power, and both are within our reach.

Victory conditions:
- When the time runs out, hold four objectives for a brilliant victory, three for a victory, two for a tactical victory.
- The objectives are Kurgan (13,14), Chashinskiy (4,7), Vargashi (25,17) and the Tobol crossing (9,24).
- Or take both of their forward positions at (39,22) and (27,29).

briliant.text:
The Tobol line is ours and their forward groups have been broken up on the near bank. That is the end of the last offensive Kolchak's armies will ever mount.

From here it is pursuit, and the only questions are how fast we can move and how much of Siberia rises in front of us. Omsk is four hundred versts away and their government is already loading its trains.

We are back over the Tobol and holding the far bank. Their groups east of the river are intact.

It has cost them more than it has cost us, which is true and is no consolation while the line is where it is.

intro:
Darkness falling: Novonikolayevsk

December 7th, 1919

Omsk fell without a fight three weeks ago. Their government left it by train and their army left it on foot, and the two have not been in the same place since.

What is in front of us now is the Great Siberian Ice March: half a million people - the remains of three armies, their families, the typhus - moving east along one railway in December, with the Czechoslovak Legion holding the line for its own trains and letting nothing else past.

Novonikolayevsk is the bridge over the Ob. Take it and the whole column east of here is cut off from the whole column west of here.

Victory conditions:
- Take the two Novonikolayevsk sectors (29,20) and (28,23).
- Hold Kolyvan (21,3), Lokti (38,5), Pavino (19,24) and the Novonikolayevsk approach (32,24).

briliant.text:
The bridge is taken. Thirty thousand prisoners and more typhus cases than anyone can count; the town's hospitals were full before we arrived and the retreating command left them as they were.

The Fifth Army is ordered to go on to Krasnoyarsk. There is a rising there already - the garrison has arrested its own officers - and the partisan armies of the Yenisei are on the railway ahead of us.

intro:
Crying souls: Krasnoyarsk

January 4th, 1920

Krasnoyarsk has taken itself.

The garrison arrested its own commander on the last day of December and the town is held by a revolutionary committee, the railway workers and Shchetinkin's partisan army out of the Yenisei taiga. Our own leading divisions are still four days behind.

Kappel's column is coming down the line towards it - what is left of three armies, on foot, in forty degrees of frost, and they have to get through this town or round it. They have nothing to lose, which makes them dangerous in a way that a supplied army is not.

Hold the city and the approaches with what is here. The partisans know this country and we do not; they are allies and they are to be treated as allies.

Victory conditions:
- When the time runs out, hold three objectives for a brilliant victory, two for a victory or a tactical victory.
- The objectives are the two Krasnoyarsk sectors (20,11), (23,12) and Drokino (18,9).
- Or take Areyskoye (11,9).

briliant.text:
The city is held. Sixty thousand men laid down their arms in and around it over three days - most of them conscripts who had been waiting for somewhere to stop.

Part of the column went round us to the north, over the Yenisei ice and into the taiga, and is heading for Irkutsk along the river. Kappel is with them. In this weather, on that route, the frost will do most of what we would have had to do.

The Fifth Army goes on east. So do I.

lose.text:
They came through the town. The committee's detachments and the partisans fought in the streets for two days and the column went east over their dead.

It is not finished. There is one more place on this railway where it can be finished, and it is Irkutsk.

intro:
Once we were here: Irkutsk

January 27th, 1920

The last of it, and it is being decided in a town that changed sides by itself.

The Political Centre rose in Irkutsk at the end of December and handed the city, and the Supreme Ruler, to the Revolutionary Committee three weeks later; the Czechoslovaks gave him up at the station in exchange for a clear road to Vladivostok for their own trains. Kolchak is in the prison here. So is the gold, or what is left of it.

Coming at us out of the taiga is what survived the march: Kappel died of frostbite and pneumonia on the road and Voitsekhovsky has the column now, and he has demanded the city, the prisoner and a contribution. Semyonov's Cossacks are east of the lake. The Baikal ice is the only way past us.

Hold Irkutsk and Listvennichnoye. Take Khomutovo, where their column is forming.

Victory conditions:
- When the time runs out, hold three objectives for a brilliant victory, two for a victory, one for a tactical victory.
- The objectives are the two Irkutsk sectors (17,8), (20,10) and Listvennichnoye (29,23).
- Or take Khomutovo (18,3).
- The enemy escapes instead if one of his columns reaches the ice road at Bolshoye Goloustnoye (40,19).

briliant.text:
Irkutsk is held. The column went round the city in the end - over the Baikal ice, in February, in a wind that took more of them than we did - and what reached Transbaikalia reached it as a crowd and not as an army.

Kolchak was shot on the seventh of February by order of the Revolutionary Committee, with Voitsekhovsky's guns within a day's march. They put him and Pepelyaev through the ice of the Ushakovka.

The Eastern Front is finished. Two years ago I was a commander of a detachment on a railway with four towns on it and no orders; tonight I am writing a report in Irkutsk and the line behind me runs unbroken to Moscow. The Far East is not ours yet and there is a buffer republic being argued about in the newspapers, but that is politics and somebody else's work.

I am going home by train. It will take eleven days and I intend to sleep for all of them.
